head.name: @fzlt/core/terrain
head.lead: A heightfield for diorama scenes. A grid of vertex heights in world units (y up, x and z the floor plane, like diorama), filled from data, a seeded noise generator (hills, or ridged dunes stretched across a wind) and stamps (bump, ramp, whoops, berm, a flat ribbon for the track), then queried for physics and drawn into a @fzlt/core/diorama scene. - Each cell is two triangles split along the same diagonal the drawing uses, so height(x, z) is exactly the surface on screen and normal(x, z, out) its face's normal; sample gives both. split: "adaptive" picks each cell's diagonal along its smaller height difference (sharp crests without stair-steps); the default keeps one fixed diagonal. - Generation is pure: integer hashing for the noise and only + − × ÷ and square roots (no sine, no cosine), so the same seed and stamps give the same heights, bit for bit, in every browser; both players of an online race drive the same course. - terrainView(d, t, opts) draws it as flat-shaded faces in diorama's painter's sort: a colour per height band, a steep band, painted kinds (the track); chunks, each culled off screen and drawn at a coarser cell further from the camera (lod), its edges stitched to the neighbour so no crack opens; blob shadows that lie on the slope. Nothing to call per frame: d.draw() runs it. No allocation per query or per draw (typed arrays; shades made once as strings). Lengths use steer's exact hypot (the builtin boxes its arguments).

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

blocks.label: NPM · @fzlt/core
blocks.code:
npm install @fzlt/core
import { terrain, terrainWindow, terrainView } from "@fzlt/core/terrain";

blocks.label: IN SHORT
blocks.code:
const t = terrain({ cols: 96, rows: 64, cell: 0.5 });
t.noise({ seed, amp: 2.2, ridge: 0.7, wind: [1, 0.3], stretch: 2.5 }); // dunes, the same in every browser
t.ribbon(loop, { width: 3.6, kind: 1 }).ramp([-3, 8], [1, 8], { height: 0.9 }); // a flat track, a jump
terrainView(d, t, { bands, kinds: ["#9c7a55"], lod: [26] }); // flat-shaded faces in d.draw()
t.sample(x, z, out); // [height, nx, ny, nz] under a wheel: the drawn triangle's

items.doc: An endless ground: a terrain of cols × rows cells that slides over the world lattice and asks fill only for the rows and columns it gains. The same queries (the same face rule) and the same terrainView; version bumps once per slide. The window decides no height (they come from fill), so where it sits is not game state. Nothing is filled until the first follow or moveTo.
